sections.title: About Badger Supports
intro: Badger Supports is a student-led community built around peer connection. Badgers come together to talk about mental health, share experiences, and support one another in everyday moments. Our peer support groups, workshops, and craft nights offer space to be heard, understood, and connected.

sections.title: Application Overview
intro: Badger Supports is funded through the General Student Services Fund administered by the Associated Students of Madison. The General Student Services Fund exists to support programs and services that directly serve the UW–Madison student community. Staffing hours are allocated based on service needs and project demands that advance student support, access, and engagement.

Badger Supports hiring process uses a generalist model, with applicants considered holistically based on interests, skills/experience, and availability. Appointments typically range from five to twelve hours per week, with additional hours assigned for time-limited or project-based work aligned with our student-focused programming.
Flat Rate of $15.15 per hour.

questions.label: Eligibility
questions.help: To be eligible for a Badger Supports Student Staff Position, you must be currently enrolled at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. If school is in a break period (summer, spring, winter), applicants must intend to enroll in courses the following semester. Review UW Policy 5003- Student Hourly Employment for more information.

sections.title: I have skills and/or interests in pursuing the following
intro: Pick skills that most resonate with you, whether that be from passion or from prior experience. We are looking for your desire to learn any of the given skills. We seek motivated, curious leaders who want to grow with the organization.

You should not limit your selections to one category, nor are you required to select all tasks within a category. If there are multiple parts to a skill and you only connect with a part of it, please still select it.

questions.label: Wellness & Support
help: The Wellness & Support Directorate develops and implements comprehensive wellness and support programs within Badger Supports. They focus on promoting mental health, well-being, and resilience among students, ensure the delivery of effective peer-support services, and manage crisis intervention as needed.
Check all that apply.

options.label: DEVELOP and/or present peer support and wellness trainings in collaboration with campus partners (UHS: Prevention and Mental Health Services)
TRAIN Peer Facilitators focused on discussion skills, prevention, and community wellness
FACILITATE check-ins and provide internal support to promote well-being and sustainability among Badger Supports members
COORDINATE and support peer support group facilitation and group processes.

questions.label: Programs
help: The Directorate of Programs designs and delivers peer led programs that foster connection, learning, and well being through shared activity. The directorate organizes craft nights and workshops that lower barriers to participation and use hands-on engagement as an entry point for peer to peer support. Programs integrate educational components that build practical skills, normalize uncertainty, and encourage conversation, creating welcoming spaces where students learn with and from one another.
Check all that apply.

options.label: DEVELOP content for NEW workshops related to mental health topics and student advocacy.
GATHER, summarize, and reflect on participant feedback

PLAN Events (Craft Nights, Open Houses, Dogs On Call, Community Art Project, etc)
CONTRIBUTE to and support the delivery of *existing* workshops

questions.label: Engagement - Outreach
help: The Directorate of Engagement, the second largest directorate at Badger Supports, advances the organization’s mission through clear, accessible, and values driven communication. The directorate leads outreach, messaging, and visual storytelling that support peer to peer engagement and promote programs and services. The directorate emphasizes leadership development in social and relational contexts, building student capacity in collaboration, audience awareness, and responsible public communication in support of a campus culture of care.
Check all that apply.

sections.title: Availability & Hours
intro: For any questions below, selected applicants will have an opportunity to discuss their responses during the interview with the organizing team.
Importantly, an appointment at Badger Supports is conditional on the accuracy of the hours requested below.

questions.label: How many Peer Support Groups per week would you feel comfortable actively facilitating?
help: Peer Support Groups are weekly, one-hour, student led spaces where participants gather for shared conversation, active listening, and mutual support. Groups focus on connection rather than advice or solutions, with facilitators helping guide discussion and maintain a supportive environment alongside trained Badger Supports volunteers.

Please answer honestly based on time availability and comfort level. If “No” or “Unsure” was selected for facilitating groups in the previous section, selecting “zero” is appropriate. Comfort with group facilitation does not affect an application, as Badger Supports values many forms of involvement and commitment.
questions.review: Google shows a linear scale from 0 to 5; here a choice of the same six numbers. Not required, as on the live form.

questions.label: Meeting Hours
questions.help: Badger Supports typically holds one organization wide meeting each month, along with weekly team meetings. On average, these meetings total approximately 1.5 to 2 hours per week.

questions.label: In addition to Peer Support Group hours and regular meetings, how many additional weekly hours would you feel comfortable taking on?
questions.help: Additional hours are primarily student facing. Examples include: preparing and delivering peer support sessions, craft nights, workshops, training, tabling, outreach, etc.

questions.label: How many hours total?
help: What is the maximum number of hours per week you are available to work, calculated as the total of the three components listed above?
Badger Supports appointments typically consist of 5-12 total hours per week.

questions.label: Active / Upcoming Commitments
help: Please provide a brief overview of your current and anticipated commitments outside of coursework for scheduling and staffing planning purposes.
Examples may include participation in student organizations, executive board roles, Greek Life involvement at a general level, or other ongoing activities.
If applicable, you may also indicate planned study abroad participation and prospective commitments, such as applying for leadership positions, joining a new club, lab, or fellowship.
Only include active/upcoming commitments, not past commitments.

For Greek Life involvement, please only indicate the level of current or planned involvement. Information regarding Greek Life and study abroad is collected for appointment purposes and generally will not affect final hiring decisions.
